Classify movement phases

Source: R/class.mov.R
class.mov.Rd

Classifies movement trajectories into distinct functional phases (i.e., ARP, Type 0, Type 1, Type 2, Type 3) based on Area-Restricted Phase (ARP) patches, spatial links, and site fidelity, based on network complexity.

Usage

class.mov(
  data,
  id.col = "ID",
  time.col = "time",
  establish = FALSE,
  establish.days = NULL,
  arp.links = "arp"
)

Arguments

data

An object of class disperseR containing movement data and linked ARP clusters.

id.col

Character. Name of the column containing individual identifiers. Default is "ID".

time.col

Character. Name of the column containing timestamp or date-time values. Default is "time".

establish

Logical. If TRUE, applies site fidelity corrections requiring a minimum duration at a ARP site to consider it established. Default is FALSE.

establish.days

Numeric. Minimum duration threshold in days for an ARP cluster to be considered an established site. Required if establish = TRUE. The duration of a stay goes from the first to the last location of consecutive ARP blocks joined by link.arp(), including the linking locations between them, so a linked ARP made of several short visits counts as one stay.

arp.links

Character. Method for evaluating links between ARPs. Either "arp" or "mcp" (Minimum Convex Polygon). Default is "arp".

  • "arp": Classifies locations sequence of ARP cluster links as ARPs.

  • "mcp": Calculates a Minimum Convex Polygon (MCP) around the points of the preceding ARP cluster. It evaluates if the sequence of ARP cluster links geometrically falls within this polygon to refine the classification. If so, they are considered ARPs. Otherwise they are considered Type 1. Requires x and y coordinate columns.

Value

An object of class disperseR with an updated dataset containing the classified phase and cluster_established columns.

Details

The movement phases follow a 0-3 hierarchy based on spatial network memory:

  • Type 0: Unanchored movement. Occurs before the first ARP is established.

  • Type 1: Loop / Local fidelity. Origin and destination ARPs are identical.

  • Type 2: Network expansion. Movement from a known ARP to a newly discovered ARP.

  • Type 3: Internal transit. Movement between two different, previously known ARPs.

Examples

eps <- get.epsilon(sim_states)
#> Computing a global threshold using all data combined.
arp <- get.arp(sim_states, epsilon = eps, delta.days = 2, pct.state1 = 0.2)
linked <- link.arp(arp, thres = 24 * 3600)

mov <- class.mov(linked)
table(mov$data$ID, mov$data$phase)
#>      
#>       ARP Type 0 Type 1 Type 2 Type 2 or Type 1 Type 3
#>   F02 629     55      0    142                0      0
#>   F04 649     54    130      0                0      0
#>   F05 159    161      0      0              129      0
#>   M01 854     63     72    103                0     95
#>   M03 364     55      0     74                0      0

# Require at least 3 days in an ARP for it to count as established
mov_est <- class.mov(linked, establish = TRUE, establish.days = 3)
table(mov_est$data$ID, mov_est$data$phase)
#>      
#>       ARP Type 0 Type 1 Type 2 Type 2 or Type 1 Type 3
#>   F02 557     55      0    214                0      0
#>   F04 649     54    130      0                0      0
#>   F05 159    161      0      0              129      0
#>   M01 854     63     72    103                0     95
#>   M03 364     55      0     74                0      0
